matches.rationale: No finding addresses the absence of statistical variability or confidence intervals in the abstract's claim about 14.6% improvement. The findings focus on table cross-references, numeric inconsistencies across specific tables, and a citation year mismatch, none of which relate to the abstract's overstatement of results.

The ground truth identifies a fabricated 1892 reference (Filippini); the only citation-related findings are a wrong table number in an appendix and a 2022/2023 year mismatch for a different author, neither of which captures the fabrication issue.
No finding identifies the inconsistency about how the difference-based action embedding from Section 3.2 is integrated into the loss or prediction heads described in Sections 3.1/3.3.

The ground truth concerns missing hyperparameter tuning details for baselines, undermining fair comparison. No finding mentions baseline reimplementation, hyperparameter tuning, or experimental fairness.

This ground truth flags missing variance/confidence intervals in Table 1. While Finding 2 mentions t-tests in an appendix, it points to a wrong table reference, not the absence of variability in the main results table. The scientific issue differs.
The ground truth concerns ethical transparency and lack of bias/failure-mode discussion in the conclusion. None of the findings address ethical considerations, biases, or responsible AI deployment.

This cross-section inconsistency between ground-truth vs. pseudo labels across sections is not identified by any finding; the findings are about table numeric discrepancies, a cross-reference error, and a bibliographic year slip.

Ground truth flags overly promotional rhetoric in the introduction ('powerful', 'promising pathway'). No finding reports rhetorical presentation manipulation or inflated language in any part of the paper.
Finding 1 concerns a numeric mismatch between Table 5 and main tables, not the suspiciously flat performance across concept counts in Table 4. The observed issue differs.
None of the findings discuss privileged information usage, realistic evaluation scenarios, or potential label leakage in the experimental design.
The disproportionate training times (8 hrs vs 30 min) between datasets is not remarked upon in any finding; the findings discuss unrelated numeric inconsistencies and reference errors.
No finding addresses the missing criteria or thresholds for VLM-based frame filtering mentioned in Section 3.1; the findings focus elsewhere.
The mismatch between claimed multi-action generalization and single-action evaluation is not identified. No finding deals with this misrepresentation of demonstrated capabilities.

The conclusion's exaggerated rhetoric about future integration into foundation models and downstream tasks is not flagged by any finding. The findings are about data/citation errors, not rhetorical overreach.

No finding points out the undiscussed large precision drops for baseline models in Table 2(b), nor suggests cherry-picking or incomplete evaluation. The three findings address entirely separate issues.
